text_note.zh: 语料里有几处旧字形或异体字，这里改用通行的简体：“劒”作“剑”，“僊”作“仙”，“徴”作“征”，“氊”作“毡”，“簷”作“檐”。“十鼓祗载”的“祗”是繁简转换的错误，原字是“祇”，意思是“只”，通行本写作“只”。“愿借辨口”的“辨”，通行本作“辩”。
text_note.en: The corpus uses several old or variant character forms, here written in standard simplified form: jiàn (sword), xiān (immortal), zhēng (summon), zhān (felt) and yán (eaves). In line 40 the corpus has zhī (respectfully), a slip in the machine conversion; the original character means 'only', and the common text writes zhǐ (only). In line 64 the corpus writes biàn with the 'distinguish' character; the common text uses the 'debate' character.

readings.zh: 少陵是长安城南的地名，这里读 shào。杜甫曾住在附近，自称“少陵野老”。
readings.en: Shàolíng is a place south of Chang'an, read shào here. Du Fu lived nearby and called himself the old man of Shaoling.

readings.zh: 朝贺：朝见天子并祝贺，读 cháo。
readings.en: Here it means to go to court before the king, read cháo.

readings.zh: 山阿：山弯、山脚，读 ē，不读 ā。
readings.en: In shān ē, the foot or bend of a hill, it is read ē, not ā.
In chā é, a mistake, it is read chā.

readings.zh: 委蛇读 wēi yí，宽广从容的样子，不读 shé。
readings.en: Wēi yí means broad and easy. Here it is read yí, not shé (snake).
In xīng xiù, the stars, it is read xiù.
In hào gǔ, to love old things, it is read hào.
In duó liáng, to measure, the first word is read duó.
In duó liáng, to measure, the second word is read liáng.

readings.zh: 现在读 guò。这首诗押“歌、何、多”一类的韵，这个字在古代读平声，和它们押韵。
readings.en: Read guò today. The poem rhymes with words like gē, hé and duō; in old times this word was read in the level tone and rhymed with them.

readings.zh: 填咽：拥挤、堵塞。一般读 yè，一说读 yān。
readings.en: Tián yè means jammed and crowded. It is usually read yè; another view reads it yān.
Here it means tilted, read pō.
In zhōng cháo, the royal court, it is read cháo.

readings.zh: 著手：动手，同“着手”，读 zhuó。
readings.en: In zhuó shǒu, to set one's hand to, it is read zhuó.

readings.zh: 摩挲：用手轻轻抚摸。这里读 mó suō，和“歌、何”押韵。口语里也读 mā sa。
readings.en: Mó suō means to stroke gently. It is read mó suō here and rhymes with gē and hé. In everyday speech it is also said mā sa.

readings.zh: 那：这里是“奈何”的意思，读 nuó，和“歌、何”押韵。
readings.en: Here it means 'what can be done', read nuó, rhyming with gē and hé.

glosses.zh: 张生：姓张的读书人。一般认为是诗人张籍，一说是张彻。
glosses.en: zhāng shēng: a scholar named Zhang. Usually taken to be the poet Zhang Ji; another view says Zhang Che.

glosses.zh: 石鼓文：刻在石鼓上的文字。这里指从石鼓上拓下来的纸本。
glosses.en: shí gǔ wén: the writing carved on the Stone Drums. Here it means a paper rubbing of it.

glosses.zh: 少陵：指杜甫，他自称“少陵野老”。
glosses.en: shào líng: Du Fu, who called himself the old man of Shaoling.

glosses.zh: 谪仙：指李白。贺知章说他是从天上被贬到人间的仙人。
glosses.en: zhé xiān: Li Bai. He Zhizhang called him an immortal sent down from heaven.

glosses.zh: 才薄：才华浅薄，是谦虚的话。
glosses.en: cái bó: of small talent, a modest way to speak of oneself.

glosses.zh: 将奈石鼓何：能拿石鼓怎么办呢？意思是写不好石鼓。
glosses.en: jiāng nài shí gǔ hé: what can I do with the Stone Drums? That is: how could I write well enough about them?

glosses.zh: 周纲：周朝的统治和法度。纲，原来指渔网上的总绳，比喻国家的法纪。
glosses.en: zhōu gāng: the rule and laws of Zhou. Gāng is the main rope of a net, a picture for a state's laws.

glosses.zh: 陵迟：衰落，一天天坏下去。
glosses.en: líng chí: to decline, getting worse day by day.

glosses.zh: 四海沸：天下像开水一样翻滚，形容大乱。
glosses.en: sì hǎi fèi: the whole land boiling like water, meaning great unrest.

glosses.zh: 宣王：周宣王，西周的君王，他让衰落的周朝一度重新强盛。
glosses.en: xuān wáng: King Xuan of Zhou, a Western Zhou king who made the weakened Zhou strong again for a time.

glosses.zh: 天戈：天子的兵器，指天子的军队。
glosses.en: tiān gē: the Son of Heaven's spear, meaning the king's army.

glosses.zh: 明堂：古代天子举行大典、接见诸侯的大殿。
glosses.en: míng táng: the great hall where ancient kings held ceremonies and received the lords.

glosses.zh: 朝贺：来朝见天子，向他祝贺。
glosses.en: cháo hè: to come before the king and congratulate him.

glosses.zh: 剑佩：剑和玉佩，古代贵族挂在身上。
glosses.en: jiàn pèi: swords and jade pendants, worn by nobles in ancient times.

glosses.zh: 鸣相磨：互相碰撞摩擦，发出声音。
glosses.en: míng xiāng mó: knocking and rubbing together, making a ringing sound.

glosses.zh: 搜：打猎。
glosses.en: sōu: to hunt.

glosses.zh: 岐阳：岐山的南面，在今天的陕西。古人把山的南面叫“阳”。
glosses.en: qí yáng: the south side of Mount Qi, in today's Shaanxi. In old Chinese the south side of a hill is called yáng.

glosses.zh: 骋雄俊：让勇士和骏马尽情奔驰。
glosses.en: chěng xióng jùn: letting brave men and fine horses gallop freely.

glosses.zh: 遮罗：拦住，用网捉住。
glosses.en: zhē luó: to block in and catch with nets.

glosses.zh: 镌功勒成：把功业刻在石头上。镌、勒都是刻的意思。
glosses.en: juān gōng lè chéng: to carve the king's deeds in stone. Both juān and lè mean to carve.

glosses.zh: 告万世：告诉千秋万代的后人。
glosses.en: gào wàn shì: to tell people of all ages to come.

glosses.zh: 隳：毁坏，这里指凿开。
glosses.en: huī: to break down; here, to cut into.

glosses.zh: 嵯峨：高高的山。
glosses.en: cuó é: high, steep hills.

glosses.zh: 从臣：跟随君王的大臣。
glosses.en: cóng chén: the officials who followed the king.

glosses.zh: 咸：都。
glosses.en: xián: all.

glosses.zh: 拣选：挑选。
glosses.en: jiǎn xuǎn: to choose.

glosses.zh: 撰刻：写好文字，再刻上去。
glosses.en: zhuàn kè: to compose the words and then carve them.

glosses.zh: 山阿：山弯、山脚。
glosses.en: shān ē: the bend or foot of a hill.

glosses.zh: 炙：烤，这里指太阳暴晒。
glosses.en: zhì: to roast; here, the sun beating down.

glosses.zh: 燎：火烧。
glosses.en: liáo: to burn.

glosses.zh: 鬼物：鬼神。
glosses.en: guǐ wù: ghosts and spirits.

glosses.zh: 烦㧑呵：不停地挥手呵斥，赶走侵害。烦，劳烦，频繁。
glosses.en: fán huī hē: busily waving and shouting to drive harm away.

glosses.zh: 公：您，对张生的尊称。
glosses.en: gōng: you, sir; a polite way to address Zhang.

glosses.zh: 纸本：纸上的拓本。拓本是把纸蒙在刻字的石头上，用墨轻轻拍打，字就印到纸上。
glosses.en: zhǐ běn: a paper rubbing. To make one, you lay paper over carved stone and dab it with ink, so the words print onto the paper.

glosses.zh: 毫发尽备：连头发丝那样细小的地方都齐全。
glosses.en: háo fà jìn bèi: complete down to details as fine as a hair.

glosses.zh: 差讹：差错。
glosses.en: chā é: mistakes.

glosses.zh: 辞严义密：文辞庄重，意思严密。
glosses.en: cí yán yì mì: the words are stern and the meaning is dense.

glosses.zh: 不类：不像。
glosses.en: bù lèi: not like.

glosses.zh: 隶：隶书，汉代通行的一种字体。
glosses.en: lì: clerical script, a style of writing common in the Han dynasty.

glosses.zh: 科：蝌蚪文，一种古老的字体，笔画头粗尾细，像小蝌蚪。
glosses.en: kē: tadpole script, an ancient style whose strokes are thick at the head and thin at the tail, like tadpoles.

glosses.zh: 缺画：缺掉的笔画。
glosses.en: quē huà: missing strokes.

glosses.zh: 斫断：砍断。
glosses.en: zhuó duàn: to chop apart.

glosses.zh: 蛟鼍：蛟龙和鳄鱼。鼍，扬子鳄。这里说笔画像被砍断的活蛟龙、活鳄鱼，又有力又生动。
glosses.en: jiāo tuó: dragons and alligators. Tuó is the Chinese alligator. The strokes look like living dragons and alligators cut apart: strong and full of life.

glosses.zh: 鸾翔凤翥：鸾鸟和凤凰飞舞。鸾凤是传说中的神鸟。翥，向上飞。
glosses.en: luán xiáng fèng zhù: the luan bird and the phoenix soaring. Both are birds of legend. Zhù means to fly upward.

glosses.zh: 众仙下：许多仙人从天上降下来。
glosses.en: zhòng xiān xià: many immortals coming down from the sky.

glosses.zh: 珊瑚碧树：珊瑚和碧玉做的树，都是珍宝。
glosses.en: shān hú bì shù: trees of coral and green jade, both treasures.

glosses.zh: 交枝柯：树枝互相交错。柯，树枝。
glosses.en: jiāo zhī kē: branches crossing each other. Kē means a branch.

glosses.zh: 金绳铁索：金做的绳子，铁做的链子。
glosses.en: jīn shéng tiě suǒ: ropes of gold and chains of iron.

glosses.zh: 锁纽：锁扣和绳结。
glosses.en: suǒ niǔ: locks and knots.

glosses.zh: 古鼎跃水：古鼎从水里跳出来。一般认为用了周朝宝鼎沉在泗水里的传说。鼎，古代煮东西、祭祀用的大铜器。
glosses.en: gǔ dǐng yuè shuǐ: an ancient cauldron leaping out of the water. It is usually taken to use the legend of a Zhou treasure cauldron sunk in the Si River. A dǐng is a large bronze vessel for cooking and offerings.

glosses.zh: 龙腾梭：梭子变成龙飞走。传说晋朝陶侃得到一只织布梭，挂在墙上，后来变成龙飞走了。梭，织布时来回穿线的工具。
glosses.en: lóng téng suō: a shuttle turning into a flying dragon. Legend says Tao Kan of the Jin dynasty found a weaving shuttle and hung it on his wall, and it later turned into a dragon and flew away. A shuttle carries the thread back and forth in weaving.

glosses.zh: 陋儒：见识浅陋的读书人。
glosses.en: lòu rú: narrow-minded scholars.

glosses.zh: 编诗：编《诗经》。《诗经》是中国最早的诗歌总集。
glosses.en: biān shī: compiling the Book of Songs, the earliest Chinese collection of poems.

glosses.zh: 二雅：《诗经》里的《大雅》和《小雅》。
glosses.en: èr yǎ: the Greater Odes and Lesser Odes, two parts of the Book of Songs.

glosses.zh: 褊迫：狭窄。
glosses.en: biǎn pò: cramped, narrow.

glosses.zh: 委蛇：宽广从容的样子。
glosses.en: wēi yí: broad and at ease.

glosses.zh: 孔子西行不到秦：相传《诗经》是孔子整理的。孔子周游各国，没有往西到秦地，所以没见到石鼓。
glosses.en: kǒng zǐ xī xíng bù dào qín: legend says Confucius edited the Book of Songs. He traveled to many states but never went west to Qin, so he never saw the drums.

glosses.zh: 掎摭：拾取、收集。
glosses.en: jǐ zhí: to pick up and gather.

glosses.zh: 星宿：星星。
glosses.en: xīng xiù: the stars.

glosses.zh: 遗羲娥：漏掉了太阳和月亮。羲，羲和，神话里替太阳赶车的神；娥，嫦娥，住在月亮上。比喻收了小的，漏了最宝贵的石鼓。
glosses.en: yí xī é: leaving out the sun and the moon. Xīhé drives the sun's chariot in myth, and Chang'e lives on the moon. It means he kept small things but missed the most precious one, the drums.

glosses.zh: 嗟予：唉，我呀。
glosses.en: jiē yú: alas, I.

glosses.zh: 好古：爱好古代的东西。
glosses.en: hào gǔ: loving ancient things.

glosses.zh: 生苦晚：可惜生得太晚。
glosses.en: shēng kǔ wǎn: sadly born too late.

glosses.zh: 涕泪：眼泪。
glosses.en: tì lèi: tears.

glosses.zh: 滂沱：雨下得很大的样子，这里形容泪流不止。
glosses.en: pāng tuó: pouring like heavy rain; here, tears that will not stop.

glosses.zh: 蒙：承蒙，受到。
glosses.en: méng: to receive, to be honored with.

glosses.zh: 博士：这里指国子博士，在国家最高学府教书的官。
glosses.en: bó shì: here, an Erudite, an official who taught at the nation's highest school.

glosses.zh: 征：征召，朝廷叫人去做官。
glosses.en: zhēng: to be summoned by the court to serve.

glosses.zh: 元和：唐宪宗的年号。元和元年是公元806年。
glosses.en: yuán hé: the reign name of Emperor Xianzong of Tang. Its first year was 806.

glosses.zh: 故人：老朋友。
glosses.en: gù rén: an old friend.

glosses.zh: 右辅：一般认为指长安西边的凤翔一带，石鼓就在那里。
glosses.en: yòu fǔ: usually taken to mean the Fengxiang area west of Chang'an, where the drums were.

glosses.zh: 度量：测量。
glosses.en: duó liáng: to measure.

glosses.zh: 掘臼科：挖好安放石鼓的坑。臼科，坑。
glosses.en: jué jiù kē: to dig pits to set the drums in.

glosses.zh: 濯冠沐浴：洗干净帽子，洗头洗澡，表示郑重。
glosses.en: zhuó guān mù yù: washing one's hat and bathing, to show great respect.

glosses.zh: 祭酒：国子监的长官，相当于国家最高学府的校长。
glosses.en: jì jiǔ: the head of the national academy, like the principal of the nation's highest school.

glosses.zh: 至宝：最珍贵的宝物。
glosses.en: zhì bǎo: the greatest treasure.

glosses.zh: 存岂多：留存下来的哪会多呢？
glosses.en: cún qǐ duō: how many could have survived?

glosses.zh: 毡包席裹：用毡子包，用席子裹。毡，用羊毛压成的厚片。
glosses.en: zhān bāo xí guǒ: wrapped in felt and woven mats. Felt is a thick sheet pressed from wool.

glosses.zh: 立致：马上运到。
glosses.en: lì zhì: brought at once.

glosses.zh: 只载数骆驼：只要几匹骆驼就能驮完。
glosses.en: zhǐ zài shù luò tuó: only a few camels are needed to carry them.

glosses.zh: 荐诸：把它献到。荐，进献。
glosses.en: jiàn zhū: to offer them to.

glosses.zh: 太庙：皇帝祭祀祖先的庙。
glosses.en: tài miào: the temple where the emperor honored his ancestors.

glosses.zh: 郜鼎：郜国的大鼎。春秋时鲁桓公从宋国得到它，放进了太庙。
glosses.en: gào dǐng: the great cauldron of the state of Gao. In the Spring and Autumn period Duke Huan of Lu got it from Song and placed it in his ancestral temple.

glosses.zh: 光价：光彩和价值。
glosses.en: guāng jià: glory and worth.

glosses.zh: 岂止百倍过：何止超过一百倍。
glosses.en: qǐ zhǐ bǎi bèi guò: far more than a hundred times greater.

glosses.zh: 圣恩：皇帝的恩典。
glosses.en: shèng ēn: the emperor's kindness.

glosses.zh: 太学：国家最高学府。
glosses.en: tài xué: the Imperial Academy, the nation's highest school.

glosses.zh: 诸生：学生们。
glosses.en: zhū shēng: the students.

glosses.zh: 切磋：原指加工骨头、象牙，这里指一起研究讨论。
glosses.en: qiē cuō: first meaning to carve bone and ivory; here, to study and discuss together.

glosses.zh: 观经鸿都：去鸿都看石经。东汉时在洛阳把儒家经书刻在石碑上，来看、来抄的人非常多。鸿都，东汉洛阳的鸿都门，这里借指那个地方。
glosses.en: guān jīng hóng dōu: going to Hongdu to see the stone classics. In the Eastern Han, the Confucian classics were carved on stone tablets in Luoyang, and huge crowds came to see and copy them. Hongdu was a gate in Luoyang, used here for that place.

glosses.zh: 填咽：拥挤、堵塞。
glosses.en: tián yè: jammed and crowded.

glosses.zh: 坐见：眼看着就能见到。
glosses.en: zuò jiàn: would surely see.

glosses.zh: 奔波：奔走而来。
glosses.en: bēn bō: rushing here.

glosses.zh: 剜苔剔藓：挖掉、剔去石头上的青苔。
glosses.en: wān tái tī xiǎn: scraping the moss off the stone.

glosses.zh: 节角：笔画的棱角。
glosses.en: jié jiǎo: the edges and corners of the strokes.

glosses.zh: 妥帖：稳稳当当。
glosses.en: tuǒ tiē: firm and steady.

glosses.zh: 平不颇：放平，不歪斜。颇，偏、歪。
glosses.en: píng bù pō: level, not tilting.

glosses.zh: 大厦深檐：大房子，深深的屋檐。
glosses.en: dà shà shēn yán: a big hall with deep eaves.

glosses.zh: 盖覆：遮盖保护。
glosses.en: gài fù: to cover and protect.

glosses.zh: 期：希望。
glosses.en: qī: to hope.

glosses.zh: 无佗：没有意外。佗，同“他”，别的事故。
glosses.en: wú tuó: nothing going wrong.

glosses.zh: 中朝：朝廷里。
glosses.en: zhōng cháo: at the royal court.

glosses.zh: 老于事：办事老练，这里有圆滑、怕麻烦的意思。
glosses.en: lǎo yú shì: seasoned in affairs; here it hints they were slippery and avoided trouble.

glosses.zh: 讵肯：哪里肯。
glosses.en: jù kěn: how would they be willing?

glosses.zh: 感激：被打动而奋发起来。
glosses.en: gǎn jī: to be moved into action.

glosses.zh: 媕婀：犹豫不决，拿不定主意。
glosses.en: ān ē: to hesitate and never decide.

glosses.zh: 敲火：在石头上敲打取火。
glosses.en: qiāo huǒ: striking sparks on the stone to make fire.

glosses.zh: 砺角：磨角。
glosses.en: lì jiǎo: rubbing horns.

glosses.zh: 著手：动手，伸手。
glosses.en: zhuó shǒu: to put one's hand on.

glosses.zh: 摩挲：用手轻轻抚摸。
glosses.en: mó suō: to stroke gently.

glosses.zh: 日销月铄：一天天、一月月地被消磨。铄，熔化、损耗。
glosses.en: rì xiāo yuè shuò: wearing away day by day and month by month.

glosses.zh: 就埋没：快要被埋没了。
glosses.en: jiù mái mò: about to be lost and forgotten.

glosses.zh: 西顾：向西边望。石鼓在西边。
glosses.en: xī gù: to look west, where the drums were.

glosses.zh: 吟哦：吟诗。
glosses.en: yín é: to chant poems.

glosses.zh: 羲之：王羲之，东晋大书法家，被称为“书圣”。
glosses.en: xī zhī: Wang Xizhi, the great calligrapher of the Eastern Jin, called the Sage of Calligraphy.

glosses.zh: 俗书：世俗流行的书法。这是韩愈拿它和古老的石鼓文比较时说的。
glosses.en: sú shū: popular writing. Han Yu says this when comparing it with the ancient drum script.

glosses.zh: 趁姿媚：追求漂亮好看。
glosses.en: chèn zī mèi: chasing prettiness.

glosses.zh: 博白鹅：换来白鹅。传说王羲之喜欢鹅，有个道士请他写经书，用一群鹅作交换。
glosses.en: bó bái é: to trade for white geese. Legend says Wang Xizhi loved geese, and a Daoist gave him a flock in exchange for copying a book.

glosses.zh: 继周八代：周朝以后的八个朝代，泛指周以后的历代王朝。
glosses.en: jì zhōu bā dài: the eight dynasties after Zhou, meaning all the dynasties since.

glosses.zh: 争战罢：战争已经停了。
glosses.en: zhēng zhàn bà: the wars are over.

glosses.zh: 收拾：收集整理。
glosses.en: shōu shí: to gather and care for.

glosses.zh: 理则那：这是什么道理呢？那，就是“奈何”，怎么办。
glosses.en: lǐ zé nuó: what is the reason for this? Nuó means 'what can be done'.

glosses.zh: 方今：如今。
glosses.en: fāng jīn: now.

glosses.zh: 柄任：重用。柄，权柄。
glosses.en: bǐng rèn: to rely on and give power to.

glosses.zh: 儒术：儒家的学问。
glosses.en: rú shù: Confucian learning.

glosses.zh: 丘轲：孔丘（孔子）和孟轲（孟子）。
glosses.en: qiū kē: Kong Qiu (Confucius) and Meng Ke (Mencius).

glosses.zh: 上论列：向朝廷上奏，一条一条地陈述。
glosses.en: shàng lùn liè: to present to the court and argue point by point.

glosses.zh: 辩口：能说会道的口才。
glosses.en: biàn kǒu: an eloquent tongue.

glosses.zh: 如悬河：像瀑布一样滔滔不绝。悬河，从高处挂下来的河，就是瀑布。
glosses.en: rú xuán hé: flowing like a waterfall. A hanging river is a waterfall.

glosses.zh: 止于此：就到这里为止。
glosses.en: zhǐ yú cǐ: ends here.

glosses.zh: 呜呼：唉，表示感叹。
glosses.en: wū hū: alas.

glosses.zh: 蹉跎：落空，白白耽误。
glosses.en: cuō tuó: to come to nothing, wasted.

translation.zh: 张生拿着石鼓文的拓本来找我，
translation.en: Mr. Zhang came to me holding a rubbing of the Stone Drum writing.

translation.zh: 劝我试着写一首《石鼓歌》。
translation.en: He urged me to try writing a Song of the Stone Drums.

translation.zh: 可杜甫已经不在，李白也已去世，
translation.en: But Du Fu is gone, and Li Bai is dead too.

translation.zh: 我才学浅薄，拿这石鼓怎么办呢？
translation.en: With my small talent, how can I do the drums justice?

translation.zh: 周朝的统治衰落了，天下乱得像开水在翻滚。
translation.en: The rule of Zhou had decayed, and the whole land boiled with unrest.

translation.zh: 周宣王愤然而起，挥动天子的兵器去平乱。
translation.en: King Xuan rose in anger and swung the Son of Heaven's spear.

translation.zh: 他大开明堂，接受诸侯的朝拜和祝贺。
translation.en: He threw open the Bright Hall and received the lords who came to bow and congratulate him.

translation.zh: 诸侯身上的剑和玉佩互相碰撞，叮当作响。
translation.en: The lords' swords and jade pendants knocked together and rang.

translation.zh: 他在岐山南面打猎，勇士骏马尽情奔驰。
translation.en: He hunted south of Mount Qi, and his bold riders galloped.

translation.zh: 方圆万里的鸟兽，都被围住、网住。
translation.en: Birds and beasts for ten thousand li were all hemmed in and netted.

translation.zh: 他把功业刻下来，好告诉千秋万代。
translation.en: He had his deeds carved, so that all later ages would know.

translation.zh: 于是凿开高高的山石，做成石鼓。
translation.en: So stone was cut from the high cliffs and shaped into drums.

translation.zh: 跟随他的大臣，才华都是第一流的。
translation.en: The officials who followed him were all of the highest talent.

translation.zh: 挑选好的人写好文字刻上去，把石鼓留在山脚。
translation.en: The best were chosen to write and carve the words, and the drums were left at the foot of the hills.

translation.zh: 石鼓经受着雨打、日晒和野火烧，
translation.en: Rain beat on them, the sun baked them, and wildfires swept over them.

translation.zh: 有鬼神守护着，不停地赶走侵害。
translation.en: Spirits guarded them, always driving harm away.

translation.zh: 先生，你是从哪里得到这份纸上的拓本的？
translation.en: Sir, where did you get this paper copy?

translation.zh: 连头发丝那样细的地方都齐全，没有一点差错。
translation.en: Every hair-thin detail is there, without a single mistake.

translation.zh: 文辞庄重，意思紧密，读起来很难懂。
translation.en: The words are stern and the meaning dense; it is hard to understand.

translation.zh: 字体既不像隶书，也不像蝌蚪文。
translation.en: The script looks like neither clerical script nor tadpole script.

translation.zh: 年代久远，难免有缺了笔画的地方。
translation.en: After so many years, of course some strokes are missing.

translation.zh: 那笔画像快剑砍断的活蛟龙、活鳄鱼，
translation.en: The strokes look like live dragons and alligators cut apart by a sharp sword,

translation.zh: 又像鸾凤飞舞，众仙人从天而降，
translation.en: Or like phoenixes soaring and a crowd of immortals coming down,

translation.zh: 又像珊瑚和碧玉树，枝条互相交错，
translation.en: Or like coral and green jade trees with their branches crossing,

translation.zh: 又像金绳铁索，绳结粗壮结实，
translation.en: Or like golden ropes and iron chains locked in strong knots,

translation.zh: 又像古鼎跃出水面，又像梭子化成龙飞腾。
translation.en: Or like an ancient cauldron leaping from the water, or a shuttle turning into a flying dragon.

translation.zh: 见识浅陋的儒生编《诗经》时，没有把它收进去，
translation.en: Narrow-minded scholars who compiled the Book of Songs left it out,

translation.zh: 使得《大雅》《小雅》显得狭窄，不够宽广从容。
translation.en: So the Odes seem cramped, without breadth and ease.

translation.zh: 孔子往西走，没有到过秦地，
translation.en: Confucius traveled west but never reached the land of Qin.

translation.zh: 他捡了天上的星星，却漏掉了太阳和月亮。
translation.en: He gathered the stars but missed the sun and the moon.

translation.zh: 唉，我爱好古物，可惜生得太晚了，
translation.en: Alas, I love ancient things, but I was born too late.

translation.zh: 对着它，我的眼泪像大雨一样流下来。
translation.en: Facing it, my tears pour down like heavy rain.

translation.zh: 记得当年我刚被召去做国子博士，
translation.en: I remember when I was first called to be an Erudite at the academy.

translation.zh: 那一年刚刚改了年号，叫作元和。
translation.en: That was the year the reign name changed to Yuanhe.

translation.zh: 我的老朋友在右辅一带的军中做事，
translation.en: An old friend of mine was serving in the army in the Youfu region.

translation.zh: 他替我量好地方，挖好了安放石鼓的坑。
translation.en: He measured the ground for me and dug pits to set the drums in.

translation.zh: 我洗净帽子、沐浴更衣，郑重地去报告祭酒：
translation.en: I washed my hat, bathed, and solemnly went to tell the head of the academy:

translation.zh: 像这样的宝贝，世上还能留下多少？
translation.en: How many treasures like this are left in the world?

translation.zh: 用毡子包、席子裹，马上就能运来；
translation.en: Wrapped in felt and mats, they could be brought here at once;

translation.zh: 十个石鼓，只要几匹骆驼就能驮完。
translation.en: The ten drums would need only a few camels to carry.

translation.zh: 把它献到太庙，可以和郜鼎相比，
translation.en: Offered to the ancestral temple, they would rank with the Gao cauldron,

translation.zh: 它的光彩和价值，何止超过百倍！
translation.en: And their glory and worth would be far more than a hundred times greater!

translation.zh: 皇上如果开恩，允许把它留在太学，
translation.en: If the emperor kindly let them stay at the Imperial Academy,

translation.zh: 学生们就能一起讲解，互相研究。
translation.en: The students could explain them and study them together.

translation.zh: 当年在鸿都看石经的人，还挤得道路都堵住了，
translation.en: Long ago, crowds jammed the roads to see the stone classics at Hongdu;

translation.zh: 眼看全国的人都会赶来观看。
translation.en: We would surely see people from all over the country rushing here.

translation.zh: 挖掉青苔，剔去藓，露出笔画的棱角，
translation.en: Scrape off the moss and lichen, and the edges of the strokes would show;

translation.zh: 把石鼓安放稳当，平平正正，不歪不斜，
translation.en: Set the drums firmly in place, level and not tilting;

translation.zh: 用大房子和深屋檐把它们盖好护住，
translation.en: Cover them with a big hall and deep eaves,

translation.zh: 希望经过很久很久，也不出意外。
translation.en: And hope that through the long ages nothing goes wrong.

translation.zh: 可是朝中的大官们，办事老练又圆滑，
translation.en: But the high officials at court were old hands, careful to avoid trouble.

translation.zh: 哪里肯被打动？只是含含糊糊，拿不定主意。
translation.en: How could they be moved? They only hemmed and hawed.

translation.zh: 放牛的孩子在石鼓上敲石取火，牛在上面磨角，
translation.en: Herd boys strike sparks on the drums, and oxen rub their horns on them.

translation.zh: 还有谁会伸手去爱惜地抚摸它们呢？
translation.en: Who will ever lay a loving hand on them?

translation.zh: 一天天、一月月地磨损，快要被埋没了。
translation.en: Day by day, month by month, they wear away and will soon be lost.

translation.zh: 六年来我总是向西望，只能白白地吟诗叹息。
translation.en: For six years I have looked west, only chanting in vain.

translation.zh: 王羲之的字流行于世，追求的是漂亮好看，
translation.en: Wang Xizhi's popular handwriting chases prettiness,

translation.zh: 几张他写的字，还能换来一群白鹅。
translation.en: Yet a few sheets of it could be traded for white geese.

translation.zh: 周朝以后，八个朝代的战争都已结束，
translation.en: Through the dynasties after Zhou, the wars have all ended,

translation.zh: 却没有人来收拾整理石鼓，这是什么道理呢？
translation.en: Yet no one has gathered and cared for the drums. Why is that?

translation.zh: 如今天下太平，每天都没有大事，
translation.en: Now the land is at peace, with nothing troubling it day after day.

translation.zh: 朝廷重用儒学，尊崇孔子和孟子。
translation.en: The court relies on Confucian learning and honors Confucius and Mencius.

translation.zh: 我怎样才能把这件事上奏朝廷讨论呢？
translation.en: How can I bring this matter before the court?

translation.zh: 真希望能借来一张口若悬河的好嘴。
translation.en: I wish I could borrow a tongue that flows like a waterfall.

translation.zh: 我的《石鼓歌》就写到这里吧，
translation.en: My Song of the Stone Drums ends here.

translation.zh: 唉，我的心愿恐怕要落空了。
translation.en: Alas, I fear my wish will come to nothing.

background.zh: 石鼓是唐朝初年在今天陕西宝鸡一带发现的十块鼓形石头，上面刻着很古老的文字，叫石鼓文。韩愈认为它们是周宣王时刻的；现在的学者大多认为是春秋战国时秦国的刻石。元和元年（806年），韩愈做国子博士，曾请求把石鼓运到太学保护起来，没有被采纳。后来朋友张生拿来石鼓文的拓本，请他作诗，他就写了这首长诗。诗里说“六年西顾”，所以一般认为写于元和六年（811年）左右。今天，石鼓收藏在北京故宫博物院。
background.en: The Stone Drums are ten drum-shaped stones found in the early Tang near today's Baoji in Shaanxi. They are carved with very old writing, called the Stone Drum script. Han Yu believed they were made in the time of King Xuan of Zhou; most scholars today think they are carvings from the state of Qin in the Spring and Autumn or Warring States period. In 806, when Han Yu was an Erudite at the national academy, he asked for the drums to be moved to the Imperial Academy for safekeeping, but nothing was done. Later his friend Zhang brought him a rubbing of the writing and asked for a poem, and he wrote this long one. Because the poem says 'six years I have looked west', it is usually dated to around 811. Today the drums are kept in the Palace Museum in Beijing.

author_note.zh: 韩愈（768—824），字退之，唐代文学家，“唐宋八大家”之首。他提倡学习先秦两汉朴实有力的古文，反对只讲辞藻的文章。他写诗也爱用奇特的字、硬朗的句子和大段议论。这首诗里一连串奇特的比喻，正是他的风格。他尊崇儒学，所以格外看重石鼓这样的上古文物。
author_note.en: Han Yu (768–824), also called Han Tuizhi, was a Tang writer and the first of the Eight Great Prose Masters of Tang and Song. He urged people to write plain, strong prose like the ancients, not just pretty words. His poems, too, love rare words, hard-edged lines and long arguments. The chain of strange comparisons in this poem is his style. He honored Confucian learning, so he cared deeply about ancient relics like the Stone Drums.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗像一篇用诗写成的长文章，分三段。第一段讲石鼓的来历：周宣王打猎立功，凿石刻字，石鼓在山野里经历风雨，好像有鬼神守护。第二段写石鼓上的字：韩愈一口气用了好几个比喻，说笔画像被砍断的蛟龙，像飞舞的凤凰，像交错的珊瑚树，像金绳铁索，让我们“看见”这些古字的力量和生气。接着他埋怨孔子编《诗经》漏掉了它。第三段讲自己：他曾想把石鼓运到太学保护，大官们却拖着不办，石鼓只能被牧童敲打、被牛磨角。读到这里，你能感到一个爱古物的人眼看宝贝被糟蹋时的着急和心痛。最后一句“呜呼吾意其蹉跎”，是一声长长的叹息。
appreciation.en: This poem is like a long essay written in verse, in three parts. The first tells where the drums came from: King Xuan of Zhou hunted and won glory, stone was cut and carved, and the drums stood in the wild through wind and rain, as if guarded by spirits. The second part describes the writing. Han Yu piles up comparisons: the strokes are like dragons cut apart, like soaring phoenixes, like crossing coral trees, like golden ropes and iron chains. They let us 'see' the power and life of the old script. Then he complains that Confucius left it out of the Book of Songs. The third part is about himself. He once tried to move the drums to the academy to protect them, but the high officials dragged their feet, and the drums were left for herd boys to strike and oxen to rub. Here you can feel the worry and heartache of someone who loves old things and watches a treasure being ruined. The last line, 'Alas, my wish will come to nothing', is one long sigh.
